issues.detail: Error scenarios (CLI failures, authentication errors, rate limiting, no resources found) are not systematically addressed in procedural steps, only in Guidelines.
Detailed instructions and executable examples are AWS-specific; GCP and Azure are mentioned but lack equivalent command examples and cost estimation.

scenarios.name: full-aws-multi-region-audit
scenarios.rationale: Response A provides runnable AWS CLI commands for 2 of 3 required checks (describe-volumes with status filter, describe-addresses for unassociated IPs) and structure for cost estimation, but critically omits the snapshot audit with age filtering, doesn't implement costs using provided pricing ($0.08/GB gp3, $0.05/GB snapshots, $0.005/hour IPs), lacks category organization (STORAGE/NETWORK/COMPUTE) sorted by monthly savings, and never mentions AMI dependencies; Response B mentions all requirements but provides zero implementation—no commands, no calculations, no organization—and asks for permission instead of attempting the task, making it a placeholder rather than a solution.

scenarios.name: ebs-cleanup-script-generation
scenarios.rationale: Response A implements the core safety mechanisms explicitly required in the rubric—snapshots before deletion and scheduled-for-deletion tags with future dates—plus a clear three-stage execution progression (dry-run → tag → force). Response B omits both snapshots and scheduled-for-deletion tags, instead using age-based filtering without a grace period, despite offering stronger explicit warnings about data loss and attempting cost calculations; the absence of snapshots is a critical safety gap when dealing with potentially critical data.

scenarios.name: rds-rightsize-analysis
scenarios.rationale: Response A shows basic CloudWatch command structure but uses --period 3600 (hourly) instead of the required 86400 seconds (daily), and fails to recommend checking connections and IOPS before making downsizing decisions. Response B correctly implements get-metric-statistics with 86400-second period, dynamic 14-day calculation, and explicitly requires evaluating CPU, connections, and IOPS together before recommending downsizing—directly meeting all rubric requirements.
